name: Hyunmoo-3 land-attack cruise missile
overview_md:
The Hyunmoo-3 is South Korea's long-range land-attack cruise missile — the Tomahawk-class backbone of Seoul's deep-strike capability against North Korea. Named for a mythical guardian, it is a subsonic, terrain-following missile fielded in progressively longer-ranged variants (Hyunmoo-3A/B/C/D) with reach reportedly extending from around 500 km up to 1,500 km, covering the entire North Korean landmass from launchers in the South.

It forms the cruise-missile element of South Korea's three-pillar deterrent: the "Kill Chain" pre-emptive strike system, Korea Air and Missile Defense, and the Korea Massive Punishment and Retaliation concept. Guided by inertial navigation with GPS and terrain-contour matching, the Hyunmoo-3 is designed to strike hardened command bunkers, missile sites and leadership targets with precision.

For an analyst, the Hyunmoo family illustrates how a U.S. ally has built a sophisticated indigenous strike arsenal under the shadow of a nuclear-armed neighbour. The cruise-missile Hyunmoo-3 is now complemented by the very large Hyunmoo-5 ballistic "bunker-buster," giving South Korea one of the most capable conventional strike forces in Asia — a hedge that shapes deterrence on the peninsula and signals growing regional missile competition.

additional.launch_platforms: Ground TEL; ship- and submarine-launched variants

builder: LIG Nex1 / Agency for Defense Development (ADD)

combat_history.event: No combat use; central to South Korea's 'Kill Chain' and KMPR deterrent concepts.
combat_history.significance: Capability assessed from policy and testing.

modernization.description: Longer-range and submarine-launched variants alongside the new Hyunmoo-5 ballistic missile.
modernization.impact: Deepens South Korea's conventional deep-strike options.

vulnerabilities.context: Effectiveness depends on saturation and routing.

vulnerabilities.description: Cruise-missile warheads have limited penetration against deep bunkers.
vulnerabilities.context: Drove the heavy Hyunmoo-5 ballistic program.

operational_patterns.typical_deployment: Precision strikes on North Korean command, missile and leadership targets across the peninsula.
operational_patterns.typical_task_group: ROK strike units within the Kill Chain / KMPR framework.
operational_patterns.readiness_notes: Mature and fielded; range-extended variants in development.

peer_comparisons.key_differences: Hyunmoo-3 is South Korea's indigenous Tomahawk-class land-attack missile.
Comparable subsonic land-attack cruise missile in China's arsenal.
The North Korean missile threat the Hyunmoo force is built to deter and pre-empt.
peer_comparisons.video_angle: The missile race on the Korean Peninsula.

doctrine.role: Long-range land-attack cruise missile for precision deep strike against North Korean targets.
doctrine.employment: Terrain-following precision strikes on command, missile and leadership sites within Kill Chain/KMPR.
doctrine.design_philosophy: Indigenous Tomahawk-class reach to cover the entire peninsula.
doctrine.threat_context: Core of South Korea's conventional deterrent against a nuclear-armed North.
doctrine.comparison_frame: Read against the Tomahawk, China's CJ-10 and North Korea's ballistic missiles.
